notes: Honest null under rule 2, not a reachability problem - mastercardfdn.org loads fine and returned its full homepage. The problem is that every logo FILE the site serves is Mastercard Inc.'s corporate two-circles mark, while the Mastercard Foundation's own logo is an inline SVG with no probeable URL, and the two are different marks. Evidence: the Foundation's actual header lockup is an inline <svg id="bedrockja80cyrx" aria-label="20 Year Anniversary logo"> with fills #f16122, #e91d25 and #f79e1d - a three-colour anniversary mark, which is the Foundation's identity and cannot be cited because inline SVG has no src to probe. The only file assets are /assets/images/favicons/apple-touch-icon.png (180x180) and favicon-32x32.png / favicons/favicon.ico (32x32), and I rendered all three on white: each is the red-and-orange Mastercard Inc. two-circles device, not the Foundation's mark. Pixel analysis agrees the artwork is Mastercard corporate orange/red (favicon-32x32: 47.1% transparent, mean opaque rgb(239,95,32)). The Mastercard Foundation is a separate legal entity from Mastercard Inc. with its own identity, so shipping the parent's trademark against a Foundation-awarded scholarship is exactly the provenance error rule 2 exists to prevent, and I would rather report null than a plausible wrong logo per rule 7. I did not use the inline SVG as a data URI because rule 5 requires a probed URL and rule 4 requires fetching the asset, neither of which is possible for markup-embedded artwork, and constructing a data: URI would amount to fabricating an asset URL. Probed and rejected 404/410: /assets/images/logo.svg, logo.png, logos/logo.svg, logos/mastercard-foundation-logo.svg, brand/logo.svg, logo-mastercard-foundation.svg, global-header__logo.svg, favicons/favicon-192x192.png, /favicon.ico (410), /apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png (410). Also present on the page but unusable: /assets/images/favicons/android-chrome-192x192.png (200, image/png, 4224 bytes - the same two-circles device, so it fails rule 2 for the same reason), and the og:image, which points at cdn.buttercms.com, a CDN mirror of partner photography rather than a logo and a third-party host besides.
